paragraphs: The unqualified Rav Yehudah, son of Yechezkel: Halikhot Olam.

(a) Dorot Olam, Shalshelet HaKabbalah, locators 34 and 68, and Yuchasin in the sequence of tradition with Rema's glosses say he became head at Nehardea after Shmuel. Elsewhere Yuchasin, second generation of amoraim, says the end of Chavit, Asarah Yuchasin, Kiddushin 70, and Arvei Pesachim imply he was head at Pumbedita; so Rashi and Tosafot, Gittin 60b, and Rashi, Chullin 57a and Niddah 20b. Niddah 67b: he instituted a practice at Pumbedita; Chullin 110a likewise proves this, see Rami bar Temari. He is the Elder of Pumbedita; see there. He became head in 4010; Shalshelet HaKabbalah, 68a, has 4014. “Rav Yehudah died, and both academies returned to Rav Huna”; see there. Rav Sherira Gaon writes that Rav Huna presided after Shmuel, and Rav Yehudah outlived him by two years. Tosafot likewise places Rav Huna’s death before Rav Yehudah’s. See Rav Huna and the question who was greater, Rav Huna or Rav Yehudah. He was born on the day Rabbi died: Asarah Yuchasin, Kiddushin 72b. He was Rav's student and after Rav's death studied with Shmuel: Rashi, Sukkah 9a; Rashbam, beginning of Mi SheMet; see Rashi, Avodah Zarah 16b.

(b) Shmuel called him Shinnana: Berakhot 36a, “Sharp one, your view is reasonable.” It says there that although Shmuel praised him, the law follows Shmuel. So too Eruvin 28b; Shabbat 7a, 152a; Rosh Hashanah 24b; Chagigah 15b. Eruvin 54a: “Sharp one, open your mouth and read, etc.; seize and eat, for this world resembles a wedding feast.” Ketubot 14a, 53a; Kiddushin 32a; Gittin 78b; Zevachim 80b; see above. Bava Kamma 14a, near the end, 15b, 36b; Bava Batra 133b; Avodah Zarah 43b; Niddah 13a, 17a. Rav Shmuel bar Yehudah told him, “Sharp one, you told us in Shmuel's name”: Ketubot 12b. Arukh explains Shinnana as sharp, from a sharpened arrow; some say one with large teeth. He rebuked Shmuel, telling him, “One who stops his ear to a poor man's cry.” Shmuel replied, “Sharp one, your head is in cold water, but your head's head”—Mar Ukva—“is in hot water”: Shabbat 55a; see Mar Ukva. The geonim, cited in Tosafot, Bava Batra 10b, and Arukh, entry Neged, explain that he saw Shmuel seated below his student Rav Yehudah because Rav Yehudah had rebuked him as above. Hence “I saw an inverted world.” See Yosef son of R. Yehoshua ben Levi. Shmuel said of him, “This is not one born of woman”: Niddah 13a. Like R. Shimon ben Yochai, he did not interrupt Torah for prayer, saying, “People like us do not interrupt.” He prayed every thirty days; Rashi explains that he reviewed his learning every thirty days: Rosh Hashanah 35a. See R. Chiyya bar Abba. He did not walk four cubits upright. Chullin, chapter 1, 18b: R. Yosef bar Chiyya (see there) said, “I learned from Rav Yehudah, who preserves even people's uncertainties: Rav Yehudah said: R. Yirmeyah bar Abba said, uncertain whether in Rav's or Shmuel's name”; also Bekhorot 36b. Chelek and Berakhot 20a: Doeg and Achitophel asked ת״ש questions concerning a tower flying in the air [The received ת״ש is unresolved. The checked Sanhedrin gives four hundred questions and Chagigah gives three hundred.]. Rava said, “Is it an achievement to raise questions? In Rav Yehudah's years all their study was Nezikin, while we study four orders. When Rav Yehudah reached ‘A woman who presses vegetables in a pot, etc.,’ he said, ‘I see Rav's and Shmuel's difficulties.’ We teach thirteen academies, yet when Rav Yehudah took off a shoe, rain came, while we distress ourselves and no one heeds us. Rather, the Merciful One desires the heart.” Taanit 24b: his attendant Rav Kahana son of Rav Nechuni removed one shoe and rain came. He wished to remove the second, but Elijah said, “If you remove another, the Holy One, blessed be He, says: I will destroy My world.”

(c) Moed Katan 17a: a scholar had a bad reputation. Rav Yehudah asked what to do: if we ban him, the rabbis need him, since he was their local teacher; if we do not, Heaven's name is profaned. He asked Rabbah bar bar Chana whether he had heard anything concerning this. He replied, “R. Yochanan said: if the teacher resembles an angel of the Lord, seek Torah from his mouth; if not, etc.” Rav Yehudah banned him. Later Rav Yehudah fell ill. The rabbis visited, and that scholar came too. Rav Yehudah saw him and smiled. He said, “Is it not enough that you banned me? Do you also laugh at me?” He answered, “I am not laughing at you. Rather, as I go to the world to come I rejoice that I did not flatter even a great man like you.” Rav Yehudah died. The scholar came to the study house and asked to be released. They said, “No great man esteemed like Rav Yehudah is here to release you. Go to R. Yehudah Nesia”; see there. He went, and the nasi told R. Ammi to examine his case. R. Ammi considered releasing him. R. Shmuel bar Nachmani stood and said, “The sages did not treat the ban of Rabbi's maidservant lightly for three years; all the more our colleague Yehudah's.” R. Zeira said, “What has happened before us? This elder has come to the study house, though he has not come for years. Learn that release is not wanted.” He did not release him; see there.

(d) Kiddushin 70a: a man told a butcher to give him meat. He answered, “Wait until Rav Yehudah bar Yechezkel's attendant takes first.” The man said, “Who is Yehudah bar Sheviskel”—glutton? Rav Yehudah brought out a horn and banned him. They told Rav Yehudah this man habitually called people slaves. He proclaimed him a slave. The man summoned Rav Yehudah for judgment before Rav Nachman. Rav Yehudah consulted Rav Huna whether to go. He answered, “You need not go, because you are a great man”—greater than Rav Nachman, being head at Pumbedita while Rav Nachman was at Nehardea; in my opinion because the principal Babylonian academy was there, as Rashi says, Sanhedrin 32b—“but for the patriarchal house's honor, rise and go”: Rav Nachman was the exilarch's judge and the nasi's son-in-law. He found Rav Nachman making a parapet and said, “Does the Master not hold Rav Huna bar Idi's statement in Shmuel's name, that one appointed over the public may not work before three people, etc.?” See there for many such exchanges. Rav Nachman said, “Let Donag, my daughter, come and give us something to drink.” Rav Yehudah answered, “One does not make use of a woman, etc.” “Let the Master send greetings to Yalta, my wife.” He answered, “One does not inquire after a woman's welfare, etc.” Yalta sent Rav Nachman, “Release him from his dispute, lest he make you like other people. [The checked Kiddushin says ‘like the other unlearned people.’]” Rav Nachman asked why his master had come. He answered, “The Master sent a summons after me.” Rav Nachman said, “I do not know the Master's speech; would I send the Master a summons?” He took out the summons and showed him, etc. Meanwhile the man arrived and said, “You called me a slave, when I descend from the royal Hasmonean house!” He replied, “Shmuel said: anyone claiming Hasmonean descent is a slave.” Rav Nachman asked, “Does the Master not hold R. Abba's rule: when a scholar rules, if he taught that tradition to his students in his teacher's name before the case arose, he is heeded; otherwise he is not believed to say he heard it from his teacher?” He answered, “Rav Mattana supports me.” Rav Mattana had not seen Nehardea for thirteen years, but arrived that day. Rav Yehudah asked Mattana, “Does the Master remember what Shmuel said with one foot on the bank and one on the ferry?” Mattana replied, “Shmuel said: anyone claiming Hasmonean descent is a slave, etc.” He proclaimed him a slave, etc.

(e) He was his father Rav Yechezkel's teacher; see there. He told him, “Father, do not teach it thus.” Shmuel said, “Sharp one, do not speak so to your father”; see there. He walked with Rav, with a woman before them. Rav told him, “Lift your feet away from Gehinnom.” He asked, “But did the Master not say it is permissible among upright men?” He answered, “Who says upright men like you and me? Rather, like R. Chanina bar Pappi, R. Tzadok, and Rav Kahana”: Asarah Yuchasin, Kiddushin 81a. R. Zeira saw Rav Yehudah standing at his father-in-law's doorway, in good spirits; had he asked all the world's affairs, he would have answered. He asked, “Why do goats go first, etc.?” See many matters there, Shabbat 77b.

(f) His wife had a difficult temper: Kohen Gadol and HaBa Al Yevimto, Yevamot 63b. [The checked Yevamot adds that she would readily let the matter pass.] He married a priest's daughter and fell ill. He said Aaron did not wish him joined to his descendants, and recovered: Pesachim 49a. [The checked Pesachim names R. Yehoshua and leaves the outcome unstated.] He was often seized by bulmos: Rashi, Kirah, Shabbat 37b. Rav Yehudah strained, read, and signed; Rashi explains he was old and his eyes dim: Gittin 19b. See Rabbah; Tosafot, Bekhorot 44a, says he was very old and his eyes unusual. He was tall in his generation: Niddah 24b; see Abba Shaul. Rav Sherira Gaon, as cited in Yuchasin, gives his death in year 610 of the era of contracts. Heilprin gives 4058 as the corresponding year.

(g) Rav Yehudah and Rabbah: we hold like Rav Yehudah—Mevo HaGemara of R. Shmuel HaNagid. Rav Yehudah and Rav Sheshet: the law follows Rav Sheshet; see there. Rav Yehudah and Rav Huna: the law follows Rav Huna, who was his teacher; see there.

(h) R. Abba bar Kahana, in his name. R. Abba bar Zavda said: Rav Yehudah said. Abba bar bar Chana; see there. Abba of Hagronya, in his time. “R. Abba said”; R. Abba questioned him. In Abaye's name: Shabbat 57b, so too Rif and Asheri. This requires investigation: Abaye and Rava were of an age (see there), and Rava was born when Rav Yehudah died. Further, in old age Abaye married the daughter of Issi son of Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehudah after she had been widowed from two husbands. It must be the earlier Abaye; see Ulla. “Avimi said.” R. Avin and Rabbah, sons of Rav Adda, his student. He told R. Avin son of Rav Nachman, “My brother.” R. Avin of Nashkaya. Adda the surveyor said, etc. Adda Dayyala, his student. On bar Immi said to him. R. Oshaya, his student, whom he called “my son.” “Rav Acha bar Adda said: Rav Yehudah said.” “Rav Idi bar Avin said: Rav Yehudah said.” Immi, Shmuel's father, in his name. R. Inyai bar Pazi, in his name. Ammi the oven-maker. Issi, his grandson; see above. Rav Yehudah said: Rav Assi said—Yevamot 16b. Rashi there, 17a: Rav Yehudah said in Rav Assi's name, and after R. Assi's death came to Shmuel, according to Maharshal's reading. The new Talmud editions have Rav Assi saying: Rav Yehudah said. Ashyan bar Nadbakh, in his name. “The earlier Rav Ashi said.” “Rav Ashi bar Avin said: Rav Yehudah said.” Rav Bivi, in his name. Rav Beruna raised a contradiction for him. R. Berekhiah, in his name. Rav Dimi bar Yitzchak before him. Rav Huna, his colleague; some say his teacher. Rav Huna bar Yehudah said to him. Rav Hamnuna before him. R. Zavda, R. Abba's father, his student. R. Zeira; see above. Rav Zutra bar Tuvyah. R. Zeira, in his name. “Zeiri said.” R. Zeira bar Chanina, in his name. R. Zerika, in his name. “R. Chiyya said”—Shabbat 7b; Taanit 10b. He taught Chiyya bar Rav. R. Chiyya bar Avin, in his name. R. Chiyya bar Yehudah said to him. In R. Chama of Kefar Techumin's name. Chana of Baghdad said to him. Rav Chana bar Adda, his student. Rav Chanina bar Ika, in his name. Rav Chanina bar Azka, in his name. Rav Chanan bar Abba. Chinena bar Chiyya said to him. The second R. Yehudah Nesia, his colleague; see there. His son married R. Yehudah bar Chaviva's daughter. R. Yehudah bar Ammi, in his name. R. Yehudah ben Abaye, in his name. R. Yehudah bar Oshaya, in his time. Rav Yosef, his student. Pesachim 27a, “Rav Yehudah said: Rav Yosef said: Shmuel said,” is a scribal error; perhaps it should read “Rav Yosef said: Rav Yehudah said: Shmuel said.” [That is the reading in the checked Pesachim.] Rav Yosef bar Nachmani, in his time. Rav Yitzchak, his son. R. Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta, in his time. In R. Yitzchak bar Pinchas's name. “R. Yirmeyah bar Abba said”; see above. R. Yirmeyah Biraah, in his time. In Kohen's name. Rav Kahana, his brother. The second Rav Kahana before him. Levi bar Shmuel before him. Levi bar Shmuel bar Abba the priest, in his time. R. Levi bar Simon, in his time. And R. Levi. R. Muna, in his name. R. Menasheh, his student. R. Mattana, his colleague; see above. R. Natan bar Oshaya disagrees with him. Rav Natan. R. Natan bar Ukva, in his name. In Ulla's name. Bar Kaftai. Rav, his teacher. Rav son of Rav Kahana, his student. Bava Kamma 97a, near the end, has Rava telling Rav Yehudah, “According to you.” It is a scribal error, since Rava was born when Rav Yehudah died; perhaps read Rabbah. But Rabbah was his student: how could he say “According to you”? This requires investigation. Rava called him “the elder Rav Yehudah”; see there. Rabbah, his student. Rabbah bar bar Chana; see above. Rabbah bar Yitzchak said to him. Rabbah bar Rav Adda, in his name. Rabbah bar Rav Nisvi, in his time. Rachava of Pumbedita, in his name. Rami, his brother. Rami bar Pappa. Rami bar Tamra. Shmuel, his teacher. Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yehudah. In R. Shmuel bar Shilat's name. R. Shmuel bar Abba of Hagronya before him. R. Shmuel bar Nachmani, his colleague. In R. Shimon bar Chiyya Chozaah's name.
